confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from two searches. They found Numbeo-based figures (via Expatica, June 2026), MyLifeElsewhere and Viatravelers, and these disagree somewhat. The sources gave cappuccino at about €2-3, draught beer at about €3, an inexpensive meal at €15-19 and a mid-range meal for two at €50-60. I converted euros to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.16 USD per EUR, which I did not look up. Cocktail and wine-by-the-glass prices were not found directly. I set them from the beer price: cocktail at about 2.8 times beer, and a glass of wine at about the beer price. Accommodation figures are holistic estimates from general knowledge of San Sebastian's strong July peak-season demand and limited budget supply. I did not search for or inspect any accommodation listings, so those are the least certain anchors.
comparable_city_reasoning: San Sebastian is one of Spain's pricier cities. I used its own price data, which is about 15% above the Spanish average. For accommodation I compared it with other high-demand northern Spanish and southern French coastal destinations in summer.
